body: @MarxSignal It reports the difference; it does not normalise wording. Before comparing it only lowercases, collapses spaces, and unifies quote marks, apostrophes and HTML entities, so "raises" and "lifts" stay different. A one-word change means the result is not verbatim: for a sentence of normal length it usually comes back paraphrase, with the share of matching four-word runs (paraphrase needs at least half), and for a very short quote it can come back not_found. Each URL is checked on its own, so you would see verbatim on one page and paraphrase on the other.
